title: Switchover Arbitration for Region Cutovers with Hot-Cache Priming
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a deterministic switchover arbitration layer to coordinate multi-region failovers that primes hot KV/prefix caches before traffic cutover. The goal is to reduce tail latency and error rates during region cutovers by ensuring readiness checks include cache-warmth, model-variant compatibility, and a safety quorum from cross-region observers.
overview: We currently rely on simple health probes and capacity signals to trigger region failovers. This ticket builds a multi-phase arbitration flow that: (1) elects a target region via policy (latency/cost/tier preferences), (2) performs hot-cache priming and model variant sanity validation, (3) collects readiness votes from observer agents, and (4) ramps traffic using progressive gating with hedged fallback to compatible model variants. It should integrate with Smart Routing and the Console rollouts UI.
design_notes: Arbitrator is an ephemeral coordinator per-cutover: coordinator elects leader via existing region-priority policy (weights + health + cost).
Priming step will run bounded traffic shadowing (1-5 qps) into the candidate region to populate KV cache and verify cold-start latencies for different sequence lengths.

Readiness scoring composed of: cache_warmth(0-1), model_compatibility(0-1), node_inventory_safety(0-1), recent_error_rate(0-1). Cutover allowed only if score >= 0.85 and quorum includes at least 2 healthy observers for cross-checking.

If priming fails beyond threshold, coordinator should auto-select the next policy-compatible region and issue a notify-and-abort path; do not force rollback of source region unless source degraded below graceful-evict threshold.

Traffic ramp uses exponential gates (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with min dwell times and SLO checks; hedging introduces fallback model variant at the boundary where tail latency > target or error rate > threshold.
implementation_steps: Add coordinator actor in routing service: cutover orchestration state machine and event stream for observers.
Extend health probes to expose cache_warmth metric (percent of expected KV entries primed by prefix fingerprint sampling).
Shadowing harness: implement short-lived shadow clients that replay representative requests with adjustable qps.
Observer agents: lightweight per-region processes that validate model checksum, quantization metadata, and sample generation sanity (length, token-distribution heuristics).
Integrate gating with rate-limiter and traffic router to enforce progressive ramps and hedged fallbacks.
Console integration: add a cutover visualization panel and manual abort/force toggle guarded by RBAC.
Add e2e integration tests and chaos scenarios for graceful degradation.

acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can complete a simulated cutover in staging with score>=0.85 and ramp to 100% within configured dwell times without SLO violations.
Cache_warmth metric published and visible in Console for candidate region during priming with a clear pass/fail threshold.
Shadowing run populates >80% of sampled prefixes to 'warm' state within 60s for standard workloads.
Observer agents detect mismatched model metadata and prevent cutover when any critical incompatibility is present.
Progressive ramp with hedging reduces observed tail latency compared to naive immediate cutover in at least one chaos scenario (5% improvement at p99).
Manual abort in Console stops cutover and triggers safe rollback path; RBAC prevents non-admin aborts.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE/Product/Design. Agreed on readiness score formula and quorum size (2 observers).
2026-03-04: Prototype coordinator state machine drafted; pushed branch feature/region-arb-statemachine (github.com/redwood-inference/repo/compare/feature/region-arb-statemachine).
2026-03-07: Cache_warmth exporter accepted by SRE; initial sampling probe merged (PR #7891).
2026-03-09: Shadowing harness baseline built; replicated small workload from perf-cluster and measured priming time ~48s for common prefixes.
2026-03-12: Began integration of observer agent checks; model checksum validation and quantization tag checks implemented. Initial staging cutover runs scheduled for 2026-03-15.
review_feedback: PM (Jared Liu): Ensure product exposes option to prefer lower-cost region even if priming time is longer — add parameter in rollout policy.
Design (Elena Park): Console panel needs timeline visualization for priming + gating steps and clear call-to-action on failures.
SRE (Priya Rao): Quorum size of 2 is minimal; recommend configurable quorum and alerting on observer lag.
notes: Trade-offs considered: synchronous vs async priming. We choose bounded shadowing (async) to avoid blocking existing traffic but provide stronger cache_warmth signal.
Fallback model variants: prefer same-architecture quantized variant when available to reduce semantic drift; otherwise route to next-best open model with quality monitoring enabled.

Operational playbook will include checklist items: validate observer health, confirm cache_warmth>threshold, review recent error histograms, initiate cutover with manual oversight for first 3 production events.
